'''Badanaval Venkatasubba Sreekantan''' (30 June 1925- 27 October 2019) was an Indian high-energy astrophysicist and a former associate of [[Homi J. Bhabha]] at the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR). He was also a Dr. S. Radhakrishnan Visiting Professor at the [[National Institute of Advanced Studies]], [[Bangalore]].

Known for his studies in the fields of cosmic rays, elementary particles, and high-energy X-ray astronomics, Sreekantan was an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies namely, the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] as well as the [[Maharashtra Academy of Sciences]]. He was also an associate of [[Bruno Rossi]] at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. The Government of India awarded him the [[Padma Bhushan]], India's third highest civilian honour, in 1988.

== Biography ==
[[File:Crawford Hall, University of Mysore.jpg|thumb|left|[[University of Mysore]].]]
Sreekantan hailed from a family of temple priests; he was born to Laxmi Devi and Badanaval Venkata Pandit on 30 June 1925, in the small hamlet of [[Nanjangud]], located in the erstwhile Mysore state (present day [[Karnataka]]).<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1">{{Cite journal |last=P. C. Agarwal |date=May 2015 |title=A versatile and humane scientist |url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/108/09/1731.pdf |journal=Current Science |volume=108 |issue=9 |pages=1731}}</ref> He was the fifth of eight sons and three daughters born to the Pandit couple, whose Telugu speaking ancestors had migrated from [[Andhra Pradesh]] to Karnataka. B. V. Pandit, an [[Ayurveda|Ayurvedic]] physician by profession and the formulator of ''Nanjagud Ayurvedic Dental Powder'', was scholastically inclined and maintained a home library that helped Sreekantan develop a reading habit from an early age. Sreekantan attended the local high school in Nanjangud and completed his intermediate degree course at Mysore. He secured his graduate degree in physics, with [[honours degree|honours]], in 1946 and completed his master's degree the following year, specializing in [[Wireless communication]], from [[Mysore University]].<ref name="Profile of a Scientist">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252335709 | title=Profile of a Scientist | date=2015 | access-date=12 July 2015}}</ref> He continued his studies as a research scholar at the [[Indian Institute of Science]], Bangalore, but moved to Mumbai in 1948 to the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR)<ref name="Indian Astronomical Union profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/4287/ | title=Indian Astronomical Union profile | publisher=Indian Astronomical Union | date=2015 | access-date=12 July 2015}}</ref> when [[Homi J. Bhabha]] invited him for advanced research in cosmic ray physics.<ref name="Brief Resume - B V Sreekantan">{{cite web | url=http://www.nias.res.in/docs/CV-BVSreekantan.pdf | title=Brief Resume – B V Sreekantan | publisher=National Institute of Advanced Studies | date=2015 | access-date=13 July 2015 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713230112/http://www.nias.res.in/docs/CV-BVSreekantan.pdf | archive-date=13 July 2015 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> His research at TIFR earned him a PhD from the [[University of Mumbai]] in 1954.<ref name="Indian Fellow">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N76-0793 | title=Indian Fellow | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2015 | access-date=12 July 2015 | archive-date=23 October 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023202210/http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N76-0793 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Sreekantan resided in [[Malleswaram]], a suburb of the south Indian city of [[Bengaluru]].<ref name="NASI Fellows">{{cite web|url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |title=NASI Fellows |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |date=2015 |access-date=13 July 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316043224/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |archive-date=16 March 2016  }}</ref> He married Ratna, a classical musician, in 1953; she died in 2006.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /><ref name="Profile of a Scientist" />

Sreekantan died 27 October 2019 at his home in Bangalore.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cerncourier.com/a/remembering-a-cosmic-ray-pioneer-b-v-sreekantan-1925-2019/|title=B V Sreekantan 1925–2019|date=10 January 2020}}</ref>

== Career and legacy ==
[[File:Tifr main.jpg|thumb|left|[[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]], Mumbai]]
Sreekantan stayed at TIFR for 39 years, and before his retirement from TIFR service in 1987, he served as the director of the institute from 1975.<ref name="Faculty">{{cite web | url=http://www.nias.res.in/aboutnias-people-faculty-bvsreekantan.php | title=Faculty | publisher=National Institute of Advanced Studies | date=2015 | access-date=12 July 2015 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110204085702/http://www.nias.res.in/aboutnias-people-faculty-bvsreekantan.php | archive-date=4 February 2011 | df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref name="Prof. B.V. Sreekantan">{{cite web | url=http://www.cortona-india.org/Contributors.aspx | title=Prof. B.V. Sreekantan | publisher=Cortona India | date=2015 | access-date=12 July 2015 | archive-date=13 July 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713221316/http://www.cortona-india.org/Contributors.aspx | url-status=dead }}</ref> At TIFR, he initiated many research streams in cosmic ray physics and [[astrophysics]] and the research team he established for studies in high energy cosmic rays is still active. One of his early assignments at TIFR was the study of cosmic-ray-produced [[muons]] detected deep underground and Sreekantan conducted [[Particle experiments at Kolar Gold Fields|experiments]] at [[Kolar Gold Fields|Kolar Gold Mines]] in Karnataka, for the detection of the elementary particles at 2760&nbsp;m deep. Though his experiments failed to find cosmic ray produced muons, he continued his search, which resulted in the detection of cosmic ray produced [[neutrino]]s, reportedly the first detection of the subatomic particles at such depth.<ref name="Profile of a Scientist" /> His experiments served as the base of his doctoral thesis on the intensity and angular distribution of muons at different depths, prepared under the guidance of [[Homi J. Bhabha|Homi Bhabha]].<ref name="Homi Bhabha’s Legacy">{{cite web | url=http://www.tifr.res.in/~aset/Bhabha/talk011510.html | title=Homi Bhabha's Legacy | publisher=Tata Institute of Fundamental Research | date=15 January 2010 | access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> A noted Italian experimental physicist, [[Bruno Rossi]] of [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], examined the thesis and [[Mumbai University]] awarded him PhD in 1954.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" />

Sreekantan's first stint at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1954 was when he worked with [[Bruno Rossi|Rossi]] on [[cloud chamber]]s and [[K-meson]]s.<ref name="Profile of a Scientist" /> During that trip, he visited several laboratories in the UK and France to familiarize himself with the advances in high energy physics.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /> He also visited [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] and conducted experiments on K-meson decay which resulted in the publication of three scientific papers, jointly written with [[Herbert S. Bridge]] and others. Once back at TIFR, he started a new series of balloon-borne experiments for studying cosmic X-ray sources above 20 keV which helped in the future development of X-ray detectors for X-ray astronomy missions. Three X-ray instruments developed by his group were carried on the [[Astrosat]], the first Indian multiwavelength astronomy observatory, which was launched in October 2015.<ref name="astro15">{{cite news | url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/isro-to-launch-astrosat-in-2015/article5723333.ece | title=ISRO to launch Astrosat in 2015 | journal=The Hindu | access-date=27 February 2014| date=24 February 2014 }}</ref>

Sreekantan was known to have furthered the studies of [[Homi J. Bhabha|Homi Bhabha]] and [[Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi]] on the lifespan and decay spectrum of muons. He set up his laboratory using war-surplus goods from [[World War II]] procured by TIFR as well as from other sources and with the assistance of H. L. N. Murthy, an expert in glass work, who helped him in the development of [[Geiger counter]]s, he measured the lifespan of the positive muons as 2.24±0.15 microseconds. His findings were published in the Indian journal, ''Proceedings of Indian Academy of Sciences'' in 1951.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" />

[[File:Protonshower.jpg|thumb|Cosmic ray air shower created by a 1TeV proton hitting the atmosphere 20&nbsp;km above the Earth (simulation)]]
When a joint team of [[Durham University|Durham University, UK]], [[Osaka City University]], and TIFR started experiments for studying neutrinos at a depth of 2.3&nbsp;km, Sreekantan was a part of the team which recorded 18 events of neutrino interactions in [[Rock (geology)|rock]].<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -2">{{Cite journal |last=P. C. Agarwal |date=May 2015 |title=A versatile and humane scientist 2|url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/108/09/1731.pdf |journal=Current Science |volume=108 |issue=9 |pages=1733}}</ref> He was also a member of the team that worked on the [[Grand Unification Theory]], to detect the decay of protons in subterranean environment, in the 1970s, the other members of the team included [[M. G. K. Menon]]. He assisted Homi Bhabha in the installation of two cloud chambers, ''Rani'' and ''Maharani'' at the cosmic ray laboratory in Ooty in 1954. Later, a larger cloud chamber, the largest one in India till then, and an [[Air shower (physics)|air shower]] array were also set up there, with his assistance.<ref name="Counting muons amid the 'shola' forests">{{Cite web |url=https://www.livemint.com/Leisure/9hFt3c5Fq6JLCSvk766FbN/Counting-muons-amid-the-shola-forests.html |title=Counting muons amid the 'shola' forests |last=Markandeya |first=Virat |date=14 April 2017 |website=Mint|language=en |access-date=26 December 2018}}</ref> He also designed, together with Subramanian and Ramamurthy, a [[Total absorption spectroscopy|total absorption spectrometer]] and an [[Cherenkov detector|air Cherenkov counter]], and the experiments revealed to Sreekantan and his associate, S. C. Tonwar, that increase in energy was an influential factor in the increase of nucleon-anti nucleon production cross section. Their findings have been published in Palau International Coral Reef Center (PICRC) journal in 1979.<ref name="Extensive Air Showers: High Energy Phenomena and Astrophysical Aspects">{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YnsSoQke5qMC&q=s+c+tonwar&pg=PA739 | title=Extensive Air Showers: High Energy Phenomena and Astrophysical Aspects | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media | author=Peter K. F. Grieder | year=2010 | pages=1118 | isbn=9783540769415}}</ref> Along with R. H. Vatcha, he measured ''charged to neutral (C/N) ratio for high energy hadrons in showers of 1014–1016 eV energy range''{{Refn|group=note|Directly quoted from source}} and arrived at the conclusion that ''copious production of [[baryon]]s in high energy interactions is inevitable''{{Refn|group=note|Directly quoted from source}}.<ref name="Evidence for change in the characteristics of strong interactions at ultra-high energies">{{cite journal | title=Evidence for change in the characteristics of strong interactions at ultra-high energies |author1=R H Vatcha  |author2=B V Sreekantan  |name-list-style=amp | journal=J. Phys. A: Math. Nucl. Gen. | year=1973 | volume=6 | issue=7 | pages=1067 | doi=10.1088/0305-4470/6/7/027|bibcode=1973JPhA....6.1067V}}</ref> These experiments confirmed baryon production in hadron-air nucleus collisions at 1015 eV.<ref name="Profile of a Scientist" />

As the director of the TIFR, he was instrumental in the establishment of several research centres such as [[Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education]] Mumbai, [[National Centre for Biological Sciences]] Bengaluru, [[National Centre for Radio Astrophysics]] Pune and TIFR Centre for Applicable Mathematics, Bengaluru.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /> His contributions are also reported in the expansion of the TIFR Balloon Facility at Hyderabad. It was during his tenure that the ''Pelletron Accelerator'', a joint project of the TIFR and the [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] was approved.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /> He inspired [[Govind Swarup]] to prepare the proposal for the establishment of the [[Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope]] (GMRT) at [[Khodad]], Pune.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /> It was under his directorship, TIFR staff was included in the BARC contributory health service scheme. He also initiated a staff pension scheme, the proposal for company quarters for TIFR employees, subsidised housing loans and welfare schemes for lower grade staff.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" />

After his retirement from TIFR, Sreekantan was offered the [[Indian National Science Academy|INSA]] [[Srinivasa Ramanujan]] chair which he held till 1992,<ref name="Indian Fellow" /> when he moved to the [[National Institute of Advanced Studies]] (NIAS) in Bengaluru, accepting the Radhakrishnan Visiting Professor chair.<ref name="Prof. B.V. Sreekantan" /> At NIAS, he was involved in the studies related to the application of physics and mathematical tools in processing biological systems, along with R. L. Kapur, a notable psychiatrist, and continued with the studies after the death of Kapur in 2006.<ref name="Past Faculty">{{cite web | url=http://www.nias.res.in/aboutnias-people-faculty-past-rlk.php | title=Past Faculty | publisher=NIAS | date=2015 | access-date=13 July 2015 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150105084448/http://www.nias.res.in/aboutnias-people-faculty-past-rlk.php | archive-date=5 January 2015 | df=dmy-all }}</ref>

Sreekantan was associated with several notable scientific personalities such as [[Homi J. Bhabha|Homi Bhabha]], [[M. G. K. Menon]], [[Raja Ramanna]], S. Naranan, R. L. Kapur, [[Ramanath Cowsik]], V. S. Narasimham, S. V. Damle and G. S. Gokhale.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /> He delivered many keynote addresses at national and international conferences,<ref name="Is Vacuum Biology the future of Life Sciences?">{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lFaTglUvvsI | title=Is Vacuum Biology the future of Life Sciences? | publisher=YouTube | date=1 March 2012 | access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> mentored many scientists in their doctoral research and was the author of over 300 scientific papers.<ref name="Profile of a Scientist" /><ref name="Trends in the energy dependence of strong interaction characteristics at ultra-high energies">{{cite journal | title=Trends in the energy dependence of strong interaction characteristics at ultra-high energies |author1=R H Vatcha  |author2=B V Sreekantan  |name-list-style=amp | journal=J. Phys. A: Math. Nucl. Gen. | year=1973 | volume=6 | issue=12 | pages=1990 | doi=10.1088/0305-4470/6/12/524|bibcode=1973JPhA....6.1990V| doi-access=free }}</ref> He was also credited with the publication of five books, either as the author or editor.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /><ref name="Remembering Einstein: Lectures on Physics and Astrophysics">{{cite book | title=Remembering Einstein: Lectures on Physics and Astrophysics | publisher=Oxford University Press | editor=B. V. Sreekantan  | date=May 2010 | pages=224 | isbn=978-0198064497}}</ref><ref name="Interdisciplinary Perspectives on Consciousness and the Self">{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Pg-7BAAAQBAJ&q=%22Interdisciplinary+Perspectives+on+Consciousness+and+the+Self%22 | title=Interdisciplinary Perspectives on Consciousness and the Self | publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |author1=Sangeetha Menon |author2=Anindya Sinha |author3=B. V. Sreekantan | year=2013 | pages=345 | isbn=9788132215875}}</ref><ref name="Nature's Longest Threads : New Frontiers in the Mathematics and Physics of Information in Biology">{{Cite book | title=Nature's Longest Threads : New Frontiers in the Mathematics and Physics of Information in Biology |publisher = Nature's Longest Threads: New Frontiers in the Mathematics and Physics of Information in Biology. Edited by Balakrishnan Janaki & Sreekantan B V. Published by World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd| author=Janaki Balakrishnan (Author, Editor), B V Sreekantan (Author, Editor) | date=September 2014 | pages=208 | isbn=978-9814612463|bibcode = 2014nltn.book.....B|doi = 10.1142/9204}}</ref><ref name="Science Technology and Society">{{Cite book |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/work/31986780?q&versionId=45346359 |title=Science Technology and Society |last=B.V. Sreekantan |publisher=Indian Institute of Advanced Study |year=2009 |isbn=978-81-7986-074-8}}</ref>

His studies have been documented by way of one book, ''Extensive Air Showers''<ref name="Extensive air showers">{{Cite book |author1=Sreekantan, B. V. |author2=Rao, M. V. S. |date=1998 |title=Extensive air showers |location=Singapore |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=9789810228880 |oclc=40516567}}</ref> and a number of articles.<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/2081799101_B_V_Sreekantan |title=On ResearchGate |date=23 November 2017 |access-date=23 November 2017}}</ref><ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Sreekantan=3ABadanaval_Venkata=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=6 December 2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=6 December 2017}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography – Scientific publications'' section}} He wrote a monograph on ''Cosmic Rays : Current Status and Future Directions'' for Homi Bhabha Fellowships Council (unknown if finished before his death).<ref name="Prof. B.V. Sreekantan" /> He also wrote three books namely, ''Remembering Einstein: Lectures on Physics and Astrophysics'',<ref name="Remembering Einstein : lectures on physics and astrophysics">{{Cite book |last=Sreekantan |first=B. V. |date=2010 |title=Remembering Einstein : lectures on physics and astrophysics |location=New Delhi |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780198064497 |oclc=501394980}}</ref> '' Interdisciplinary Perspectives on Consciousness and the Self''<ref name="Interdisciplinary perspectives on consciousness and the self">{{Cite book |last1=Sreekantan  |first1=B. V.  |last2=Menon  |first2=Sangeetha  |last3=Sinha  |first3=Anindya  |title=Interdisciplinary perspectives on consciousness and the self |location=New Delhi |isbn=9788132215875 |oclc=866635850|date=12 December 2013  }}</ref> and ''Nature’s Longest Threads: New Frontiers in Mathematics and Physics of Information in Biology''<ref name="Nature's longest threads : new frontiers in the mathematics and physics of information in biology">{{Cite book |last1=Balakrishnan  |first1=Janaki  |last2=Sreekantan  |first2=B. V. |title=Nature's longest threads : new frontiers in the mathematics and physics of information in biology |publisher=Nature's Longest Threads: New Frontiers in the Mathematics and Physics of Information in Biology. Edited by Balakrishnan Janaki & Sreekantan B V. Published by World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd  |isbn=9789814612463 |oclc=886539946|bibcode=2014nltn.book.....B  |year=2014  |doi=10.1142/9204  }}</ref> as well as several articles on general science topics for the propagation of science.{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography - General publications'' section}}

== Positions ==
The [[Indian Institute of Astrophysics]] (IIA), established in 1786 by [[William Petrie]],<ref name="Indian Institute of Astrophysics - A Brief History">{{cite web | url=http://www.iiap.res.in/History | title=Indian Institute of Astrophysics – A Brief History | publisher=Indian Institute of Astrophysics | date=2015 | access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> was modernised in 1960 by [[Vainu Bappu]], the renowned Indian astronomer, and Sreekantan became associated with the institute during this time.<ref name="M. K. Vainu Bappu">{{cite web | url=http://www.iiap.res.in/vbappu | title=M. K. Vainu Bappu | publisher=IIA | date=2015 | access-date=13 July 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701235039/http://www.iiap.res.in/vbappu | archive-date=1 July 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref> The institute, functioning under the [[Ministry of Civil Aviation (India)|Ministry of Civil Aviation]], was brought under the jurisdiction of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] in 1985 with the efforts of [[Raja Ramanna]] and Sreekantan, when it was made an autonomous institution.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /> He was a member of the governing council of the institute from 1988 till 2007, a total of 19 years, of which 15 years from 1992, he served as the chairman of the council.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /> It was during his tenancy as the chairman, the institute set up the [[Indian Astronomical Observatory|Himalayan Chandra Telescope]] (HCT) at Hanle, [[Ladakh]] at an altitude of 14000&nbsp;ft.<ref name="Overview">{{cite web | url=http://www.iiap.res.in/about/overview | title=Overview | publisher=IIA | date=2015 | access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> He is also credited with assisting [[Ramanath Cowsik]] with the establishment of a new campus for IIA at [[Hoskote]] in Karnataka and in the construction of housing for the staff of the institute.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" />

Sreekantan served as the visiting professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for two terms, the first from 1954 to 1955 and subsequently from 1965 to 1967.{{citation needed|date=January 2020}} He was associated with the [[University of Tokyo]] as their JSPS visiting professor in 1977 and taught at the [[University of California, Irvine]] and the [[University of California, San Diego]] during 1993–94.<ref name="Prof. B.V. Sreekantan" /> He served as the president of the Indian Physics Association (1976–78) and the physics section of the Indian Science Congress (1981). He held the post of the vice chairman of the IUPAP Cosmic Ray Commission from 1987 to 1993, sat as a member of the [[Atomic Energy Commission of India|Atomic Energy Commission]] during 1985–86 and held the chair of the Research Council of [[National Physical Laboratory of India|National Physical Laboratory]], New Delhi.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /> During 1986–88, he served as the vice president of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Present Fellows - IAS">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/listing/fellows/A |title=Present Fellows – IAS |date=10 December 2017 |website=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=10 December 2017}}</ref> He was an editorial fellow of the [[Project of History of Indian Science, Philosophy and Culture]] and chaired the ''Gandhi Centre for Science and Human Values'' of [[Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan]].<ref name="Brief Resume - B V Sreekantan" /> He also serves as the chairman of the board of directors of ''Sadvaidyasala'', an [[Ayurvedic medicine]] company<ref name="Nanjangud tooth powder usage on decline, toothpaste in the offing">{{cite web | url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mysuru/Nanjangud-tooth-powder-usage-on-decline-toothpaste-in-the-offing/articleshow/27862257.cms | title=Nanjangud tooth powder usage on decline, toothpaste in the offing | work=Times of India| date=24 December 2013 | access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> founded by his father.<ref name="Sadvaidyasala">{{cite web | url=http://sadvaidyasala.com/about.html | title=Sadvaidyasala | publisher=Sadvaidyasala | date=2015 | access-date=13 July 2015 | archive-date=30 April 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150430122845/http://sadvaidyasala.com/about.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> Much of his later scientific work involved the study of the phenomenon of [[consciousness]] and its relationship with the physical sciences.<ref name="Physics and Consciousness">{{cite web | url=http://niasconsciousnesscentre.com/BV-Sreekantan/Physics-Module.html | title=Physics and Consciousness | publisher=NIAS | date=2015 | access-date=14 July 2015}}</ref><ref name="Prof. B. V. Sreekantan, Governing Council - TERI Prakriti School">{{Cite web |url=http://www.teriprakritischool.org/b-v-sreekantan.php |title=Prof. B. V. Sreekantan, Governing Council – TERI Prakriti School |date=21 May 2018 |website=teriprakritischool.org |access-date=21 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528173846/http://www.teriprakritischool.org/b-v-sreekantan.php |archive-date=28 May 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
Sreekantan was an elected fellow of four major science academies in India; the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (1965),<ref name="IAS Fellows">{{Cite web |url=https://www.ias.ac.in/listing/fellows/S |title=IAS Fellows |date=19 May 2018 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=19 May 2018}}</ref> the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (1976),<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=9 December 2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=9 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] (1989)<ref name="NASI Year Book 2015">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI Year Book 2015 |date=24 November 2017 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=24 November 2017 |archive-date=6 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806211716/http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Maharashtra Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Profile of a Scientist" /> He is an honorary fellow of the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] and the [[Indian Institute of Astrophysics]], Bengaluru.<ref name="IIA Fellows">{{cite web | url=http://www.iiap.res.in/people/personnel_honfel.htm | title=IIA Fellows | publisher=Indian Institute of Astrophysics | date=2015 | access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> The [[University Grants Commission of India]] awarded him the [[C. V. Raman]] Award in 1977 and selected him as the [[University Grants Commission (India)|UGC]] National Lecturer in 1978, the same year as he delivered the PMS Blackett Memorial Award Lecture of INSA–[[Royal Society of London]].<ref name="Brief Resume - B V Sreekantan" /> One more award reached him in 1978, the Homi Bhabha Medal from the [[Indian National Science Academy]].<ref name="Indian Fellow" />

Four years later, the Indian Physics Association awarded Sreekantan the [[R. D. Birla]] Memorial Award.<ref name="Brief Resume - B V Sreekantan" /> He received four awards from various governments, starting with the third highest civilian honour of [[Padma Bhushan]] from the [[Government of India]] in 1988.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{Cite web |url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |title=Padma Awards |date=19 May 2018 |publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |archive-date=15 October 2015 |url-status=dead |access-date=19 May 2018 }} [https://padmaawards.gov.in/ Alt URL]</ref> The [[Indian Institute of Science]] Distinguished Alumni Award<ref name="Prof. B.V. Sreekantan" /> and the [[Ramanujan]] Award of the [[Indian Science Congress]] were awarded to him in 1987 and 1989 respectively and the [[Government of Madhya Pradesh]] awarded him the Jawaharlal Nehru Award in 1991.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" /> He was awarded the [[Rajyotsava Prashasti]] by the [[Government of Karnataka]] in 1998<ref name="Karnataka Rajyothsava 1998">{{Cite web |url=http://oldsite.nal.res.in/pdf/krarchives.pdf |title=Karnataka Rajyothsava 1998 |date=19 May 2018 |publisher=Government of Karnataka |access-date=19 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180520123912/http://oldsite.nal.res.in/pdf/krarchives.pdf |archive-date=20 May 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and six years later, the government followed it up with the [[Sir M. Visvesvaraya]] Senior Scientist State Award in 2004.<ref name="A versatile and humane scientist -1" />
